rounds.fact: Vimeo launched in 2004 and deliberately positioned itself as the artsier, higher-quality alternative to YouTube, banning gaming and vlog content in its early years to keep that focus.
Fark built its entire identity around submitting and voting on weird, funny news links, a simple format that predated Reddit's rise by several years.
Winamp's slogan 'It really whips the llama's ass' became one of the most recognizable taglines of the early MP3 era, and its skinnable interface inspired an entire community of custom designs.
Netscape's browser dominated the early web so completely that Microsoft bundling Internet Explorer with Windows to compete became the center of a landmark antitrust case.
RadioShack's website in the early 2000s tried to combine its parts-and-electronics heritage with early attempts at cell phone retail, a business mix that never quite gelled online.
